subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve elevated cron and heartbeat authority with a narrow per-job flag, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance and heartbeat tool-authority design?
rationale: The request changes the host-elevated exec trust boundary across persisted cron jobs, heartbeat configuration/files, internal event providers, upgrade behavior, and operator-approved automation, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Treat this as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat modifier provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with explicit migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Remove Internal-Source Elevation
options.body: Fail closed for cron-event and heartbeat elevated access unless maintainers intentionally preserve a separate compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Treat this as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat modifier provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent caller-scoped cron work makes joshavant the closest implementation-history owner for the scheduling provenance half of this decision.
